'''Samsung Welstory''' ({{Korean|hangul=삼성웰스토리}}) is a [[South Korea|South Korean]] food services company founded in 2013.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |title=About Us {{!}} Samsung Welstory |url=https://www.samsungwelstory.com/ |access-date=2026-01-23 |website=www.samsungwelstory.com}}</ref> It is a subsidiary of [[Samsung C&T Corporation|Samsung C&T]] and has provided services to other [[Samsung]] affiliates including [[Samsung Electronics]], [[Samsung Display]], [[Samsung Electro-Mechanics]], and [[Samsung SDI]].<ref name=":32">{{Cite web |date=2021-06-03 |title=Samsung Welstory's transfer-pricing remedy rejected by FTC |url=https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/samsung-welstorys-transferpricing-remedy-rejected-by-ftc/10683415 |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=koreajoongangdaily.joins.com |language=en|last=LEE|first=HO-JEONG}}</ref>

== History ==
[[File:Samsung_Welstory_Logo_Identity_Comparison.png|thumb|A side-by-side of Samsung Welstory logos for corporate or consumer-facing situations, introduced in 2024.]]
Samsung's food services operations date back to 1982, while the Welstory brand was launched in 2007.<ref name=":02" /> The 'Samsung Welstory' entity was spun-off from Samsung Everland in 2013 after its merger with [[Cheil Industries]]. Cheil merged with C&T the year after.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |last=Su-hyun |first=Song |date=2021-07-05 |title=[News Focus] Welstory: Food for Samsung workers or the Lees? |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/2646368 |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Herald |first=Korea |date=2013-11-04 |title=Samsung Everland to reorganize business portfolio |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/24244 |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}}</ref> In 2014, a [[Vietnam|Vietnamese]] subsidiary was established.<ref name=":02" /> A [[China|Chinese]] distribution [[joint venture]] by the name of ‘[[Shanghai]] Welstory’ was established in 2016, with a [[Japan|Japanese]] wholesaler and Chinese supplier taking minority stakes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-06-23 |title=Samsung to enter joint food venture in Shanghai |url=https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/samsung-to-enter-joint-food-venture-in-shanghai/11731535 |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=koreajoongangdaily.joins.com |language=en|last=SEO|first=JI-EUN}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=김지현 |date=2016-06-23 |title=Samsung Welstory taps into W300tr Chinese market |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/1000624 |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}}</ref>

In 2021, four Samsung affiliates were fined [[South Korean won|KRW]] 234.9 billion by the [[Fair Trade Commission (South Korea)|Fair Trade Commission]] for its deals with Welstory, which did not involve open bidding and inflated the value of the services.<ref name=":12" /><ref name=":22">{{Cite web |date=2021-06-24 |title=Five Samsung companies fined for Welstory scheme |url=https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/five-samsung-companies-fined-for-welstory-scheme/10914468 |access-date=2026-01-23 |website=koreajoongangdaily.joins.com |language=en|last=LEE|first=HO-JEONG}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=June 24, 2021 |title=Samsung Elec, affiliates fined $207 mln over cafeteria contracts |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/samsung-elec-affiliates-fined-207-mln-over-cafeteria-contracts-2021-06-24/ |work=Reuters}}</ref> The FTC rejected the companies' remedy plan.<ref name=":32" /> Investigators from the Seoul Central District Prosecutors Office raided the headquarters of Welstory and Samsung Electronics in 2022 as part of the probe.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-28 |title=Raids on Samsung Electronics and Welstory unit |url=https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/raids-on-samsung-electronics-and-welstory-unit/11801429 |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=koreajoongangdaily.joins.com |language=en|last=LEE|first=MICHAEL}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Yonhap |date=2022-03-28 |title=Prosecutors raid Samsung Electronics on suspected unfair biz practice |url=https://www.koreaherald.com/article/2827643 |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=The Korea Herald |language=en}}</ref> 

In March 2024, Welstory launched its Wellybot service, featuring a cooking robot that could produce "stews and soups for high-volume meal services."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joo-young |first=Hwang |date=2024-10-27 |title=[From the Scene] How robotics reflect shift in S. Korea's food industry |url=https://www.theinvestor.co.kr/article/3853192 |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=THE INVESTOR |language=en}}</ref> In October, Welstory signed a [[memorandum of understanding]] with Louetlang to expand its presence in Europe.<ref>{{Cite web |last=도어컴 |date=2025-10-14 |title=Louetlang and Samsung Welstory Forge Strategic Alliance to Accelerate K-Food’s Global Expansion |url=https://www.koreadaily.com/article/20251013223633226 |access-date=2026-01-27 |website=미주중앙일보 |language=ko}}</ref> In April 2026, the [[Seoul High Court]] overturned the FTC's Welstory-related fines due to insufficient evidence.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Seong-Tae |first=Kim |date=2026-04-23 |title=Court Overturns 234.9 Billion Won Fine on Samsung Welstory |url=https://en.sedaily.com/society/2026/04/23/court-overturns-2349-billion-won-fine-on-samsung-welstory |access-date=2026-05-05 |website=Seoul Economic Daily |language=en}}</ref>
